explain.say: Did you know your brain is like Velcro for bad things and a slide for good things? Bad moments stick, good ones slip away! Gratitude, which means noticing and feeling thankful for good things, helps fix that. Look at the plan: first, pause tonight.

faq.q: Why does gratitude make us feel happier?
faq.a: Our brains notice bad things more easily than good ones. Gratitude trains your brain to spot the good things too, so you feel happier and calmer.

faq.q: How can I say thank you to someone?
faq.a: Say it face to face, write a note or a card, draw a picture, or do something kind back. Saying exactly what they did makes it extra special.
asks: How do I show someone I am grateful?

faq.a: Gratitude means noticing the good things in your life and feeling thankful for them, from big things like family to tiny things like a warm drink.

faq.q: What if I had a bad day and cannot think of anything good?
faq.a: Bad days happen, and it is okay to feel sad. Tiny things count: a comfy bed, a song you like, or a hug. You do not have to pretend the bad bits did not happen.

faq.q: Do I have to feel grateful all the time?
faq.a: No. It is okay to feel sad, cross or worried. Gratitude does not mean ignoring problems; it means also noticing the good things.

facts: In a 2005 study, people who wrote down three good things every night for one week felt happier for up to six months afterwards.
Many cultures hold thanksgiving harvest festivals, such as Pongal in India, Chuseok in Korea and Thanksgiving in the USA and Canada.
